Its a bug and fix will be released in `0.2.0-alpha.16`.

Some advances:

You have a data saved by cascades in which you have multiple primary keys which are referenced to another entities one of them is saved another is not, ahh soo complex. I strongly recommend you to keep things simple and avoid confusion for the ORM, yourself and people who is going to work with your code.

Also, be careful with such expression:

```ts
  this.recipients = recipients.map(recipient => ({...recipient, message: this}));
```

resulted object is instance of Object, not Recipient. This may lead to unexpected behaviour. Its much better to simply assign message property of recipient:

```ts
recipients.forEach(recipient => recipient.message = this);
this.recipients = recipients;
```

Also you have several other issues in your code like duplicate interface names and not exported interfaces. Thanks for the good repo, it would be great if you next time create a PR with a failing test like what I did here(5361167) with your code.

body: I checked your tests and skipped them. Reason why they are failing is because cascade remove functionality is not supported. You either need to configure how foreign keys will be removed using `onDelete` flag on relations (SQL's `ON DELETE`) either by calling `remove` on everything that is "bind" to your removal entity.

> Reason why they are failing is because cascade remove functionality is not supported.

`cascade?: boolean | ("insert" | "update" | "remove")[];`

What is this `cascade: ["remove"]` that appears in the types documentation about?

Anyway this was about cascade remove, what about the third test, the one which tries to delete the Recipients themselves? When trying to perform
```
await connection.getRepository(Recipient).remove(recipient);
```
I get:
```
Internal error. Subject Recipient must have an identifier to perform operation. Please report a github issue if you face this error.
```

> What is this cascade: ["remove"] that appears in the types documentation about?

Something that needs design and implementation, but currently not supported.

> await connection.getRepository(Recipient).remove(recipient);

can you console.log(recipient) ? I guess it misses one of the primary key. It must contain `user` and `message` to finish operation.
